summary: The test framework incorrectly assumes the Temporal server must be started via `startTemporalServer()` or `startTemporalTestServer()`, preventing users from running tests with externally managed (Docker) Temporal servers.
userImpact: Users cannot run RoadRunner tests when the Temporal server is managed externally (via Docker or other means) without using a workaround.
rootCause: The code checks if member variables are null (only set by startTemporalServer/startTemporalTestServer) rather than verifying if a server is actually running, incorrectly assuming the server must be started via the Environment class.
proposedFix: Support external Temporal servers via environment variable ALLOW_EXTERNAL_TEMPORAL_PROCESS=true (mentioned in PR #724).
workaround: Use Docker to run the Temporal server separately and enable the ALLOW_EXTERNAL_TEMPORAL_PROCESS environment variable to bypass the check.
keyQuote: I do not need the `startTemporalServer()`, nor the `startTemporalTestServer()` because when I spin up the docker containers it starts the temporal server.
